Hi Julian — thanks for flagging this. Short answers up front, then options below.

1) We can accept EUR-denominated wires directly to our EU nostro — preferred for EUR invoices.
2) Intermediary/correspondent charges are normally passed through by the correspondent bank (SHA by default) which can result in a shortfall at receipt.
3) We can support either:
   - "OUR" (payer bears all charges) — safest economically but some banks won't pass full amounts to beneficiary nostros.
   - "SHA" (shared) — typical in EU domestic/EU-to-EU cross-border; your bank and our bank each take their legs.
   - "BEN" (beneficiary pays) — Redwood would receive net amounts; not recommended if you want full invoice amount delivered.

Recommended path for Acme: send EUR as an OUR or SHA instruction to the attached wire template and include the explicit correspondent/beneficiary chain below. If your bank still routes through a local clearing partner that levies a separate local clearing fee, that fee often shows up as a deduction by the correspondent and is outside our control. In that case we can either:

- Accept the net amount and issue a corrective invoice/credit for the shortfall if > €20, or
- Ask Acme to send as "OUR" and work with your bank to confirm they will absorb correspondent/clearing charges.

I've attached a proposed wire template and our current intermediary fee schedule for transparency. If you want Redwood to absorb a small, one-off deduction as a concession, let me know the expected fee and volume and I can route to finance for approval.

Next steps:
- If Acme prefers Redwood to receive the invoice gross, please send as OUR or use the exact template and include the remittance reference: RW-INV-<invoice_number>.
- If Acme will not select OUR, we will accept SHA but may invoice any material shortfalls.

Thanks — I can coordinate directly with your payments ops and/or your bank if needed.

Best,
Markus Klein

Markus — quick guidance from finance and tax:

- VAT: If Acme provides a valid EU VAT ID and the supply is B2B, invoice as 0% with reverse charge. If we issue a credit for a fee concession, the credit should mirror the VAT treatment of the original invoice (i.e., keep the reverse charge note).
- Accounting: Small concessions absorbed by Redwood should be booked as "bank fee expense" (GL 6202) if we treat them as a commercial concession. If we later re-bill the customer for the shortfall, the re-bill posts to revenue (4100) and the offsetting recon goes to the suspense account until cleared.
- Threshold: agree with your operational proposal — absorb up to €15 per transaction as a courtesy; >€15 we document and either invoice or negotiate a one-off credit with business approval.

Please confirm final wording to Acme that we will: accept EUR OUR or SHA; prefer OUR for full delivery; absorb up to €15 local clearing deduction as a courtesy (booked to 6202); invoice any shortfall > €15. Also attach the wire template and ask them to confirm the exact correspondent details before sending.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Julian / Payments team — thanks for the patience. Confirming Redwood's position and the exact steps to send the April payment: 

1) Currency and instruction
   - Preferred: send the invoice amount in EUR to our EU Nostro using the attached wire_template_acme.pdf.
   - Instruction: use OUR OR SHA; OUR preferred if your bank confirms they will not debit correspondent charges from the beneficiary amount. If uncertain, use SHA but expect potential deductions.

2) Intermediary charges policy
   - Redwood will absorb up to €15 per incoming transfer as a courtesy (we will book as bank fee expense GL 6202).
   - Any deduction > €15 will be treated as a shortfall and submitted by Redwood as an invoice adjustment (posted to revenue if re-billed) unless otherwise agreed.

3) VAT/tax
   - If Acme provides a valid EU VAT ID, invoice will be issued at 0% (reverse charge). Any credit/adjustment will carry the same VAT treatment.

4) Correspondent details
   - Please populate the attached template with the exact values from your bank for the correspondent chain. If your bank refuses to share correspondent details, send a screenshot of the outgoing payment instruction so we can trace the path on our side.

5) Remittance reference
   - IMPORTANT: include remittance reference RW-INV-<invoice_number> in the instruction so funds reconcile automatically.

If that all looks good we are ready to receive the wire. If you prefer Redwood to absorb larger recurring clearing charges, we can discuss a small monthly surcharge to cover expected volume.

Best,
